subject.title: Heartbeat skipped reason 'target-none' is misleading when delivery is disabled by default

question: Should OpenClaw preserve `reason: "target-none"` and add an additive human-readable disabled-delivery hint, or should the machine-readable reason be renamed?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but the permanent fix changes a diagnostic contract that may already be consumed by scripts or UI surfaces.

options.title: Add a hint and keep target-none
options.body: Preserve the existing machine-readable reason while adding a human-readable disabled-delivery explanation to event/status/CLI output.

options.title: Rename the reason
options.body: Change `target-none` to a clearer machine-readable reason such as `delivery-disabled`, accepting possible compatibility fallout for consumers that parse the old value.

options.title: Defer the diagnostic change
options.body: Leave the current raw reason until a broader heartbeat status contract is designed.

recommendation.title: Add a hint and keep target-none
recommendation.body: Preserve the existing machine-readable reason while adding a human-readable disabled-delivery explanation to event/status/CLI output.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the default-target-none heartbeat change that made this diagnostic visible and has the strongest history on the central files.
